clue.text: Divisions this side within Civil Service

indicators.note: within says the side word sits inside the abbreviation for the Civil Service

parts.note: this clue sits on the left-hand side of the grid, so this side is LEFT

explanation.surface: A remark about factions on this side of the Civil Service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This side' is a quirky grid reference: 1 Across starts at the left edge, so it means LEFT (27 Across, at the right, uses the same words for RIGHT).
explanation.definitionFit: Clefts are splits or fissures, a synonym for divisions.

clue.text: Castles in Spain could crumble and fall to earth, invaded by airborne infiltrator

indicators.note: invaded by means the bird goes into the middle of the other pieces
crumble tells us the letters of could break apart and re-form

parts.note: to land is to come down to the ground
the cuckoo is a bird that lays its eggs in other birds' nests, an infiltrator on the wing

explanation.surface: Grand dreams collapse and crash to the ground when a flying intruder gets in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures daydreams collapsing; 'Castles in Spain' is an old idiom for daydreams, and the cuckoo is famous for slipping its eggs into other birds' nests.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean an unrealistic, fanciful dream world.

clue.text: Don't stop so often — such travel will end up as a big party!

definitions.text: Don't stop so often — such travel will end up as a big party!

parts.words: Don't stop so often — such travel will end up as a big party!
parts.note: travel that never halts goes on and on, like a party that never finishes

explanation.surface: Advice to travellers: make fewer stops and the trip turns into one long celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on reading the word as 'end less', i.e. stop less often, alongside its plain sense of never finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that ends less and less ultimately goes on without limit, never finishing.

clue.text: Drag queen — after time it's boring

indicators.note: after says the queen's letter comes behind the time letter

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
an awl is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A drag queen comes on late, and the act is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag queen' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Drag' is the definition and 'queen' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: To trawl is to drag a net through water to catch fish.

clue.text: Conrad is terribly dry

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the two words are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A verdict that the novelist Joseph Conrad is a very dry read.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry humour is mocking and understated, close to sardonic.

clue.text: Aid operation? That's about right — and right again

definitions.text: Aid operation? That's about right — and right again

indicators.note: about says the first word wraps round a letter for right

parts.note: a second R for right

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that relief delivery is correct, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own words supply the pieces: AID goes 'about' R, then another R ('right again'), then OP for operation.
explanation.definitionFit: An airdrop delivers relief supplies by parachute, a classic aid operation.

clue.text: Pluck dead duck after making slip with its head

indicators.note: after says the duck pieces come behind the slipping piece

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in family trees
erring means making a mistake or slip

indicators.note: with its head means the duck keeps its own first letter in front

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Someone plucks a dead duck after a slip-up with its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck gives O (a cricket duck is zero) 'with its head', the D at the front of duck, so DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is daring courage, a sense of pluck.

clue.text: Salt egg with ceremony

parts.note: a nit is a louse egg
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A recipe direction: salt the egg with due ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrite is a salt of nitrous acid, a chemistry sense of salt.

clue.text: Loth to go in, but not taking much pressing

definitions.meaning: a cricketer goes in to bat at the crease, so one loth to go in resists the crease
describes fabric that resists wrinkles and needs little ironing

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to go in, who doesn't need much persuading otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batter's line is the crease, so being reluctant to go in to bat is cryptically being resistant to the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistant means loth, and creasing is where a batter stands; wrinkle-proof cloth needs little ironing.

clue.text: Former secret police extracting confession from Italian inmate in POW camp

indicators.note: extracting says the Italian word is pulled out of the police name

parts.note: the Stasi was the secret police of former East Germany
si is Italian for yes, an admission
a lag is a convict, an old lag being a long-term prisoner

explanation.surface: An East German interrogator gets an Italian prisoner to talk in a wartime camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracting' takes SI out of STASI, leaving STA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for ordinary soldiers.

clue.text: Classic pic of star involved with model

indicators.note: involved here means tangled together, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A celebrity photo of a star together with a model.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a classic painting by a great European artist of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Prime of Elland Road's turn to draw — and get United again!

indicators.note: turn says the two leading letters are swapped round backwards
prime of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for road
a tie is a drawn match

explanation.surface: Leeds United's ground hosts a draw, and the team rally again.
explanation.walkthrough: Elland Road is the home ground of Leeds United, an English football club; 'turn' reverses E plus R to give RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie is to fasten or bind back together, a play on uniting once more.

clue.text: Live premiere of Diva — can you dig it?

indicators.note: premiere of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a well is something you dig

explanation.surface: A diva's opening night, and a hip question about whether you like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can you dig it?' sounds like hippie slang for 'do you like it?', but it describes a thing that is dug.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live or reside somewhere.

clue.text: Fosters louts, perhaps, left with family in care of Lewis's other 'alf

indicators.note: in care of says the family word is held inside the island word

parts.note: Lewis and Harris is one Hebridean island; its other half is Harris, dropping the H as the cockney 'alf does
kin means family

explanation.surface: Australian lager drinkers, rowdy ones, left with relatives in the care of a Hebridean.
explanation.walkthrough: Foster's is an Australian beer, so 'Fosters louts' are Australian louts. Lewis and Harris is a Scottish island; the cockney 'alf signals dropping the H of Harris.
explanation.definitionFit: Larrikin is Australian slang for a rowdy hooligan.

clue.text: Took off on sun baked breather

indicators.note: baked suggests cooking the letters into a new shape

parts.note: a lung is the organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: Someone stripped off to bake on the beach for a breather.
explanation.definitionFit: Unslung means took down something carried on a sling, such as a rifle or bag.

clue.text: Pure uranium, only mixed with lead

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of only and lead are stirred together

explanation.surface: A chemist describes uranium blended with lead alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two fodder words ONLY and LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Unalloyed means unmixed, without any impurity.

clue.text: Aspire to change, taking on Government mess

indicators.note: taking on means the anagram takes in an extra letter
to change says the letters of aspire are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ambitions for reform in government turn into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's ear is a botched job, a mess.

clue.text: Swedes into unnamed white supremacists and Jewish mysticism

indicators.note: into says the pop group goes inside the trimmed group
unnamed means the letter for name is left out

parts.note: the Klan is the Ku Klux Klan, white supremacists
ABBA were a Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: Swedish pop stars join an anonymous racist group and take up mysticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' drops N (name) from KLAN, leaving KLA, which ABBA goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kabbala is a Jewish mystical tradition interpreting scripture.

clue.text: What infected one after lift in vehicle?

definitions.text: What infected one after lift in vehicle?

indicators.note: after says the sick pieces follow the turned vehicle
lift in a down clue reads the vehicle upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle
ill means sick, infected
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question about what made someone sick after taking a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' turns CAB upwards in this down clue to give BAC. The whole clue doubles as the definition: germs caught from a lift are what infected one.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, germs that cause infection.

clue.text: Shellfish for sailor on desert island?

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
someone on a desert island is alone

explanation.surface: A castaway sailor eats seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: An abalone is an edible sea mollusc, a type of shellfish.

clue.text: More pointless Bush exercises — Pentagon reduced by 20 per cent, perhaps?

definitions.text: Pentagon reduced by 20 per cent, perhaps?

indicators.note: exercises suggests the letters are worked about into a new order
pointless means losing a compass point, here east

explanation.surface: More futile manoeuvres by President Bush as the Pentagon budget is cut by a fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' drops E (east, a compass point) from MORE, leaving MOR; 'exercises' shuffles MOR with BUSH. A five-sided shape losing a fifth of its sides has four.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a four-sided figure, one side fewer than a five-sided shape.

clue.text: Fried potatoes and eggs? It's coming up!

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means read from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: A breakfast order: fried potatoes and eggs, coming right up.
explanation.definitionFit: Roesti is a Swiss dish of grated fried potatoes.

clue.text: Us hunter's best friend could be Afghan following kite, perhaps

indicators.note: following says the hound comes after the bird

parts.note: a kite is a bird of prey
an Afghan is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: An American hunter's best companion might be an Afghan hound chasing a kite.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird dog is an American hunting dog trained to find game birds.

clue.text: Vibrate, reverberating in Service supplied by ATS, PO metallic sound

indicators.note: reverberating suggests echoing back, so the run of letters is read in reverse
in says the letters sit inside the words of the closing phrase

explanation.surface: A clatter of noise echoing round a military service provided by wartime women's corps and petty officers.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards through 'metallic sound'. ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army corps; the service words decorate the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to swing back and forth, to vibrate.

clue.text: Ultimate in danger — Prince behind a screen

indicators.note: behind says those letters come after the single letter
ultimate in means the last letter of the following word

parts.note: a ras is an Ethiopian prince or chief

explanation.surface: Peril at the end, as a prince hides behind a curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: Polonius is stabbed behind an arras in Hamlet, so the prince hiding there fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a tapestry hung as a wall screen or curtain.

clue.text: Harbouring half-formed hate

indicators.note: formed suggests the letters are shaped into a new word
half here means the first five of the word's ten letters

explanation.surface: Someone nursing a vague, undeveloped loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-formed' gives two signals: take half of HARBOURING (HARBO) and form those letters anew.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to detest or loathe.

clue.text: A horse changing direction halfway — so like our best-laid schemes!

indicators.note: the right letter in the middle is changed into the letter for left

parts.note: a grey is a grey-coated horse

explanation.surface: A quotation-laden aside about a horse veering mid-course, like our plans.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes Robert Burns, the Scottish poet: 'the best laid schemes o' mice an' men gang aft agley', i.e. often go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Agley is Scots for awry or off course, as plans often go in the poem.

clue.text: Oh dear, cat's off solids

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Dismay that the cat is off its food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oh dear, cat's off' looks like an owner's worry about a pet off its food; 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Octahedra are eight-faced geometric solids.

clue.text: Air conducted by Lord finished with a diminuendo?

parts.note: D stands for Dominus, Latin for Lord
wind is moving air
led means conducted or guided

explanation.surface: An aria directed by a nobleman ends quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conducted' and 'diminuendo' suggest music, but the conducting is plain leading, and the definition means simply grew smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwindled means diminished gradually, as a diminuendo fades in volume.

clue.text: Sunny this side — east of Britain

indicators.note: east of means placed to the right, so after the Britain letters

parts.note: Britain gives B
this clue sits on the right-hand side of the grid, so this side is RIGHT

explanation.surface: A weather report: sunshine on the eastern side of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This side' is a grid reference: 27 Across ends at the right edge, so it means RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright weather is clear and full of sunshine.
